title: Formik
description: Complete form solution with validation and state management.

data.text: Formik handles form state, validation, and submission in React with a declarative API.

data.title: Formik example

data.text: Formik keeps the whole form in one values object and tracks which fields the user has touched, so errors are shown only after a field is visited. `validate` returns an errors object, and `handleSubmit` receives the values only when there are none.

data.title: A Formik form with field-level validation

data.text: Formik pairs with Yup through `validationSchema`, which keeps rules out of the component. `<FieldArray>` handles dynamic lists such as line items, and `<FastField>` limits a rerender to a single input on large forms. Everything is controlled, which is the source of both its clarity and its cost.

data.title: A Formik form with a Yup schema
Interview angle: how Formik compares to React Hook Form
data.text: Formik stores values in React state and rerenders on every keystroke, which is simple to reason about but slower on large forms. React Hook Form keeps values in refs and rerenders less. Both are valid; the honest answer is that Formik is clearer for small, controlled forms and React Hook Form scales better. Being able to say that, with the reason, is what makes the answer strong.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Formik manages form state and submission.
